result.title: MAGMA-Bench: Evaluating Long-Horizon Embodied Agents under Dynamic Tasks and Execution Failures
result.summary: Long-horizon embodied agents must maintain task-relevant information, coordinate heterogeneous robots, and adapt their decisions as execution unfolds. Existing benchmarks investigate dynamic task execution and embodied multi-agent coordination, but provide limited evaluation of their intersection. We introduce MAGMA-Bench, an architecture-agnostic benchmark for persistent task reasoning in dynamic multi-robot environments. MAGMA-Bench evaluates agents across increasing task horizons and controlled online perturbations, including execution failures, task interruptions, and mission updates, with scenarios requiring coordination across robots with heterogeneous capabilities. It uses a structured skill-level interface to separate task-level reasoning from perception and low-level control. We evaluate locally deployable open-weight planners, multi-agent state-tracking strategies, and frontier models. Even the strongest evaluated models fail on a substantial fraction of clean episodes, and their success rates decrease further under online perturbations. Supervised adaptation greatly improves a small model, but performance remains substantially lower on longer and multi-robot missions. We release the benchmark, 261,646 task-level training examples, and an architecture-agnostic expert-trace generation pipeline.

AI.brief_summary: MAGMA-Bench 是一个架构无关的基准，评测长时程具身多机器人在动态任务、执行失败与任务中途更新下的持续任务推理，并提供技能级接口、26 万余条任务级训练样例与专家轨迹生成管线，同时对比多种开源与前沿规划器的表现。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「持续任务推理」、多智能体状态跟踪策略与扰动下的失败恢复/任务更新，可能与 LVR 中推理状态的长时程维持、长度泛化与停止决策形成概念类比，可作为待核查线索；但技能级接口把任务级推理与感知、底层控制分离，与视觉 latent 推理的直接联系有限。
